answer: An adversary who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the vault history. Churn is counted in shale, and walnut publishes the ratio each epoch. At most 25% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. A 436 account operation therefore ties up 1 million dollars of idle capital. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
